newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt gets FDA okay for molybdenum.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt gets FDA okay for molybdenum.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc said Thursday it had received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to supply U.S. customers with molybdenum manufactured at its facility in Petten, the Netherlands.
Molybdenum is a metallic element used to produce technetium for nuclear medicine. Technetium is a key component in medical imaging diagnoses, Mallinckrodt said.
Malinckrodt said limited production has already begun at the Petten facility, and output will be scaled up during the next several months.
The FDA clearance became effective June 18, it added.

"With this approval, we can now supply all our needs for this urgent material for the foreseeable future," David Morra, president of Mallinckrodt's Nuclear Medicine Division, said in a statement. "There also is a significant cost benefit for the company since we will no longer need to purchase molybdenum from other suppliers."
